Who founded the Danish royal line?
column2: Shield Sheafson, a foundling who became a conquering king, founded the Danish royal line.

column1: What is the name of Hrothgar's mead-hall?
column2: Hrothgar's mead-hall is called Heorot.

column1: Why does Grendel hate the noise in Heorot?
column2: Grendel, an outcast from God, is tormented by the sound of feasting and the scop's song about God's creation.

column1: From whom is Grendel descended?
column2: Grendel is descended from Cain, the biblical murderer whom God cursed for killing Abel.

column1: Why can the Danes not settle Grendel's feud?
column2: Grendel will never make peace or pay the death-price, so the usual way of ending a feud is impossible.

column1: Where do the Danes turn for help in their despair?
column2: The Danes make offerings at pagan shrines, because they do not know the Christian God.

column1: How does Beowulf learn about Grendel?
column2: Sailors bring stories of Hrothgar's troubles back to Geatland.

column1: Who first challenges the Geats in Denmark?
column2: The Danish coast-guard rides down to the beach and demands to know who they are.

column1: Who is Beowulf's father?
column2: Beowulf's father is Ecgtheow, a famous warrior whom Hrothgar once helped.

column1: Who is Beowulf's lord?
column2: Beowulf's lord is Hygelac, king of the Geats.

column1: Who announces the Geats to Hrothgar?
column2: Wulfgar, Hrothgar's herald, announces the Geats to the king.

column1: Why does Beowulf refuse to use a sword against Grendel?
column2: Because Grendel fights without weapons, Beowulf wants a fair fight that will bring more fame to Hygelac.

column1: What does Beowulf want sent to Hygelac if he dies?
column2: Beowulf wants his mail shirt, made by Weland and given to him by Hrethel, sent back to Hygelac.

column1: Who taunts Beowulf at the feast?
column2: Unferth, son of Ecglaf, taunts Beowulf out of envy.

column1: What contest does Unferth bring up?
column2: Unferth brings up Beowulf's swimming match against Breca on the open sea.

column1: How does Unferth say the swimming match ended?
column2: Unferth says Breca outswam Beowulf and made good his boast.

column1: How does Beowulf say the swimming match ended?
column2: Beowulf says storms drove them apart and he killed sea monsters before landing in Finland.

column1: What saves Beowulf when a sea monster drags him down?
column2: His hand-forged mail shirt protects him until he can kill the beast with his sword.

column1: What shameful act does Beowulf accuse Unferth of?
column2: Beowulf accuses Unferth of killing his own brothers.

column1: Why does Beowulf say Grendel is not afraid of the Danes?
column2: Beowulf says Grendel knows the Danes will never take revenge, so he kills them without fear.

column1: Who carries the mead cup through Heorot?
column2: Queen Wealhtheow carries the cup, first to Hrothgar and then to the rest of the company.

column1: What does Beowulf vow to Wealhtheow?
column2: Beowulf vows that he will do what the Danes need or die in the mead-hall.

column1: What does Grendel do before he reaches Beowulf?
column2: Grendel seizes a sleeping Geat and eats him whole.

column1: How does Beowulf defeat Grendel?
column2: Beowulf grips Grendel's hand until his arm tears off at the shoulder.

column1: What trophy is hung in Heorot?
column2: Grendel's arm and shoulder are hung high under Heorot's roof.

column1: Where does Grendel go to die?
column2: Grendel flees to his mere in the fens and dies there.

column1: Which hero does the scop compare Beowulf to?
column2: The scop compares Beowulf to Sigemund, the famous dragon-slayer.

column1: Which king does the scop contrast with Beowulf?
column2: The scop contrasts Beowulf with Heremod, a king who became evil and a burden to his people.

column1: What does Hrothgar promise Beowulf after the victory?
column2: Hrothgar promises to love Beowulf as a son and to give him anything he wants.

column1: What story does the scop tell at the victory feast?
column2: The scop tells the story of Finn and Hengest, a feud between the Frisians and the Danes.

column1: Who is Hildeburh?
column2: Hildeburh is Finn's queen, who loses her brother and her son in the fight at Finn's hall.

column1: Who will later wear the torque that Wealhtheow gives Beowulf?
column2: Hygelac will wear the torque on the raid in which he dies.

column1: What does "unlocked his word-hoard" mean?
column2: It means that Beowulf began to speak.

column1: What kenning for the sea appears in the opening lines?
column2: The poem calls the sea the "whale-road."

column1: Is Beowulf a folk epic or an art epic?
column2: Beowulf is a folk epic, because it grew out of oral tradition and its author is unknown.

column1: What are three examples of art epics?
column2: The Aeneid, the Divine Comedy, and Paradise Lost are art epics written by single authors.

column1: What holds a line of Old English poetry together instead of rhyme?
column2: Alliteration across the two half-lines holds each line together.

column1: Which sound alliterates in "Then a powerful demon, a prowler through the dark"?
column2: The p sound alliterates in "powerful" and "prowler."

column1: What are three kennings for the sea in Part 1?
column2: Part 1 calls the sea the "whale-road," the "swan's road," and the "wave-vat."

column1: Why does Beowulf contain both pagan and Christian elements?
column2: A Christian poet wrote down an older pagan story, so both sets of values appear.

column1: What does the king owe his thanes in the comitatus?
column2: The king owes his thanes land, wealth, and the spoils of war.

column1: What do thanes owe their king in the comitatus?
column2: Thanes owe their king loyalty, protection, and revenge if he is killed.

column1: What is the greatest disgrace in the heroic world?
column2: Disloyalty to one's lord is the greatest disgrace.

column1: What is the greatest misfortune in the heroic world?
column2: Having no lord or family is the greatest misfortune.

column1: How is the comitatus broken at the start of the poem?
column2: Hrothgar cannot protect his thanes from Grendel, so the bond of protection has failed.

column1: Why does the poet give away the ending through foretelling?
column2: Foretelling creates a sense of doom and irony, since the audience knows the outcome while the characters do not.

column1: What is an example of foretelling in Part 1?
column2: The poet foretells that Heorot will one day burn in a feud between in-laws.

column1: How should a name like Hrothgar be pronounced?
column2: Every letter is pronounced, including the H at the start of Hrothgar.
